correctness.rationale: A 106-character complete witness is explicitly given and every one of its 106 cyclic windows is checked nonpalindromic. Two separate standard-language implementations verify all 5565 unordered pairs differ both directly and under reversal, including cyclic wraparound; the formal definition therefore gives existence. No claim of global optimality or extrapolation is made.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior bounds 88<=M_4(4)<=112 neither imply nor refute M_4(4)>=106; the new witness implies the prior 88 lower bound and improves it. We do not conclude equality with 106 nor contradict the proven 112 upper bound.

originality.rationale: The exact matching parameter row of the 2025 primary paper reports a largest known period of 88, whereas the embedded 106-cycle certifies a stronger lower bound by direct inspection; that paper does not contain a covering 106-cycle. Relevant 2024 constructions and nonbinary bounds do not imply the new witness. A later/unindexed equivalent or stronger construction remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Search and indexed literature are not exhaustive: a newer, unindexed, or differently named cycle of period >=106 may exist.

value.rationale: The exact small-parameter case k=4,n=4 is explicitly open between constructive period 88 and theoretical ceiling 112 in Mitchell-Wild 2025 Table 7. An explicit period 106 closes 18 of the 24 units of this gap and gives an immediately verifiable bidirectional position-sensing cycle. This is a substantive 75-percent reduction of the specific documented gap, not a routine renaming.
